# Fixed native sources

p-net v0.2.0 commit `3e650720850e1f31f8a419c8aa135a2e81b44ddb`, OSAL `88784fcfff7a1b74e20bdeb71a55c2cdd22b4a59`, and cmake-tools `45c751c60d75bbad5eb327624c259cc02b6564b2` are original public archives, verified by `sources.lock.json`. No private reference or old executable is included. p-net's GPLv3 option applies to the native executable and thin application. OSAL and cmake-tools retain BSD notices. The GPL text and original license files accompany the full archives.

`native/profinet/build.py` extracts the public sources, supplies the fixed cmake-tools/OSAL dependencies offline, and replaces only the sample application's entry point with this project's GPL thin application. The p-net protocol library files are unchanged. The thin app's fixed-version native ABI guard validates known store files before native initialization, exposes true native current/nonvolatile memory, and records software LED callbacks. It does not implement DCP or fix/rewrite native ACK behavior. Python PTCP is an autonomous finite software profile; upstream p-net PTCP is not claimed.

The prepared compiler image is a build input, not a runtime dependency or protocol workspace. The runtime is a digest-locked public CPython image plus newly compiled native executable and project Python code; base OS copyright files remain in place. Build cache availability is explicit. An offline runtime archive import does not need to import compiler input or replace any other protocol image. Source rebuilding requires the prepared compiler input from the asset build-input archive, or explicitly preparing an equivalent public toolchain; it is not claimed bit-for-bit reproducible across arbitrary compilers.
